proposed_from.topic:
Sharp unknown-history minimax frontier for globally stable longitudinal incremental interventions. For all integers n>=1,T>=1 and known c in [0,1], observe n iid complete trajectories O=(X1,A1,...,XT,AT,Y), all Xt and At binary and Y in [0,1]. Let Ht=(X1,A1,...,X_(t-1),A_(t-1),Xt). The law class P_T includes every trajectory law on this sample space, with arbitrary history-dependent covariate, action and outcome kernels. For causal interpretation impose consistency and sequential exchangeability (no hidden treatment confounding); no missingness, Markov, smoothness, sparsity or positive treatment-probability floor is imposed. The data analyst knows n,T,c and the alphabet, and is not supplied any true kernel. Define pi_t(Ht)=P(At=1|Ht), eta=c/sqrt(T), delta=exp(eta), and q_t(P)(1|Ht)=delta*pi_t/[1+(delta-1)*pi_t]. Replace all action kernels by q_t(P), retaining covariate/outcome kernels. Let psi_T(P,c) be the resulting terminal mean. This intervened law is dominated by P, so conditional versions on P-null histories do not change psi. Deterministic treatment and null histories are included. Determine explicit evaluable functions r(n,T,c) and ell(n,T,c), up to universal multiplicative constants independent of n,T,c, for R(n,T,c)=inf_{all measurable estimators} sup_{P in P_T} E_P[(hatpsi-psi_T(P,c))^2] and L(n,T,c)=inf_{I} sup_{P in P_T} E_P[length(I)], where I is a measurable connected interval in [0,1], with optional independent randomization, satisfying inf_{P in P_T} P_P(psi_T(P,c) in I)>=0.95. Prove matching upper and lower bounds uniformly for every n,T,c, including saturation, shrinking c, and all logarithmic transition factors. Upper results must supply total finite-data algorithms for an estimator and such an interval, with stated computational cost; converses range over all estimators/intervals on the original iid experiment and the same P_T. Derive necessary and sufficient conditions for uniform consistency along sequences T=T_n,c=c_n and characterize exactly when knowing the complete propensity tree changes the order of risk or honest length. At c=0 recover R of order 1/n and L of order 1/sqrt(n). The known-propensity benchmark is uniformly order 1/n and 1/sqrt(n) for all T,c in the domain. Whether or where unknown propensities create a strict penalty is answer-open, not assumed. Exact rates, transitions, estimator algebra and proof mechanics are outputs. A fixed-T EIF, oracle-only bound, unmatched rate bracket, or illustrative impossibility example does not satisfy the kernel. Consumer: Kim, Kennedy and Naimi, Incremental Intervention Effects in Studies with Dropout and Many Timepoints (2021), analyze EAGeR aspirin adherence and pregnancy across many weeks; the mtpverse/imtp software implements incremental interventions with learned treatment propensities. The theorem would establish whether increasing the history length requires more subjects or structural restrictions even when the oracle weights have bounded second moment, informing how these workflows justify estimation precision for long histories. This binary, completely observed experiment is an explicitly restricted theoretical benchmark, not a numerical sample-size prescription for their richer covariate/dropout analysis. Sources https://arxiv.org/pdf/1907.04004 and https://github.com/mtpverse/imtp . PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A bounded presolve derived more than the known-propensity variance calculation. Complement-paired context priors make every deterministic-history intervention mean exactly one-half, while randomized late actions shift a majority outcome. Their observed-data mixtures agree whenever sampled contexts occupy different pairs, producing a sparse-history lower mechanism without random-target concentration. A natural-mean estimator with an explicit deterministic intervention-bias envelope supplies a matching long-history upper route. The full-law influence function also has a dimension-independent second-moment bound, separating local efficiency from uniform sparse-history difficulty. Independent finite enumeration checked the paired-target identity, nonuniform early intervention weights, and small-mixture likelihoods; finite differences checked the influence formula. These checks are not proofs of uniform bounds or the full frontier. Deterministic actions, null histories, zero and shrinking intervention strength, and recent static incremental/OPE comparators were considered.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Close the sharp intermediate-history transition through a compatible prefix-probability approximation/variance theorem and matching all-procedure converse, including connected honest-interval length; endpoint results must not replace this requirement.
EARLY KILL TEST: Audit the k=1,r=2 paired model and two-action prefix functional: verify mixture indistinguishability, shifted pair cancellation, and nonidentity with a static tilt, then identify the first mixed-prefix correction absent from prior theorems. Stop and re-gate if the witness fails or an existing exact reduction supplies the entire frontier.

proposed_from.novelty_justification: The closest causal paper proves identification and fixed-horizon efficiency and asks a many-timepoint precision question only through a constant-propensity variance ratio. The closest natural-policy paper compares local efficiency bounds under structured policy models. The closest finite-sample minimax papers treat one-stage fixed targets or one-time discrete adjustment. The selected kernel instead asks for one explicit all-\(n,T,c\) frontier for an endogenous sequential intervention over every compatible binary history tree, jointly matching point risk and honest connected-interval length and characterizing the exact value of knowing the full propensity tree. Its non-verbatim content is certified by the static-tilt counterexample and by the first mixed-prefix obstruction: factorial contributions share descendant counts and must obey parent-sum identities. The long-history paired-mixture theorem and the bounded centered influence function provide direct evidence that the problem is neither a routine oracle variance calculation nor a generic unseen-cell restatement.

seed_details.seed: Sharp all-sample minimax risk and honest-length frontier for the unrestricted longitudinal incremental mean
seed_details.anchor_opened: arXiv:1907.04004, Introduction, identification Theorem 3.1 and its g-formula construction, efficient influence-function Theorem 4.1 and Appendix F, growing-horizon Theorem 6.1 and Appendix F.3, and the concluding discussion.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the constant-propensity variance calculation in Theorem 6.1 by a finite-tree decision problem; the first new step is a compatible approximation theorem for the centered rational prefix functional, not an influence-function expansion.
seed_details.destination_search: Exact searches for longitudinal incremental minimax history-tree learning and propensity-dependent prefix polynomial estimation found fixed-horizon incremental theory, static continuous tilts, structured natural-policy efficiency, and one-stage discrete or bandit minimax results, but no full target theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from KimKennedyNaimi2021 because the incremental weight has a uniformly bounded second moment under \(c/\sqrt T\).
seed_details.rebuttal: A bounded oracle weight controls estimation when the propensity tree is supplied; the complement-paired mixture gives a global unknown-law penalty while the full-law influence-function norm remains bounded.

seed_details.seed: Compatible-prefix polynomial and factorial estimator for the intermediate-history regime
seed_details.anchor_opened: arXiv:2101.07781, Introduction, known- and unknown-policy Theorems 1--3, switch-estimator convex program, Chebyshev construction around equation (64), its low-count bias-variance proof, and the concluding proof section.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the per-arm Poisson unbiased-moment identity by a recursion on unconditional child masses whose factorial statistics share descendants and therefore require a nested covariance theorem.
seed_details.destination_search: JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015, RobinsLiTchetgenVanderVaart2016TR, and ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024Discrete provide adjacent polynomial, higher-order, and causal collision threads; none treats a target weight made from the same compatible prefix probabilities being estimated.
seed_details.red_team: A direct tensor product of one-dimensional Chebyshev polynomials and factorial moments solves every node independently.
seed_details.rebuttal: Prefix counts are sums of common leaf counts, child errors propagate through later normalizers, and independent nodewise approximation violates both parent-sum compatibility and the needed variance accounting.

seed_details.seed: Exact oracle-information phase diagram for behavior-dependent longitudinal policies
seed_details.anchor_opened: arXiv:2006.03886, Introduction, Definitions 1--2, tilting-policy Theorem 2, non-Markov Theorems 8--11, Algorithm 1, nuisance remainder analysis, and the proof of the efficiency-bound comparison.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the tangent-space comparison of supplied and estimated behavior policies by a finite-experiment comparison in which the target itself changes with every unknown prefix propensity.
seed_details.destination_search: MaZhuJiaoWainwright2022 supplies a one-stage oracle gap, HiranoImbensRidder2003 supplies the opposite estimated-score efficiency phenomenon, and ZhouHannaZhuYangShi2025 supplies a parametric history-length bias-variance decomposition; no source gives necessary and sufficient order separation for the present endogenous sequential policy.
seed_details.red_team: The oracle gap is already determined by the larger natural-policy efficiency bound in KallusUehara2024NaturalPolicies.
seed_details.rebuttal: Both local efficiency bounds can be uniformly bounded while global minimax risk separates, so a tangent-space variance ratio does not determine the sparse-history phase boundary.

seed_details.seed: Shortest finite-sample honest connected interval by trajectory-mixture modulus inversion
seed_details.anchor_opened: arXiv:math/0503662, Introduction, Theorem 1 lower bound, Section 2 interval construction, and Section 2.3 discussion of expected-length adaptation.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the Gaussian ordered modulus of a linear functional over convex classes by an iid trajectory-mixture modulus for a nonlinear finite-tree functional, then separately exploit interval connectedness to transfer two coverage events.
seed_details.destination_search: KimKennedyNaimi2021 gives asymptotic nuisance-controlled intervals, DaiEtAl2020CoinDICE gives Markov estimating-equation intervals, and Armstrong--Kolesar bias-aware theory assumes smooth regression classes; none minimizes expected connected length over the unrestricted trajectory simplex.
seed_details.red_team: The optimal interval length is automatically the square root of minimax mean-squared risk.
seed_details.rebuttal: That conversion is false without a confidence procedure and a coverage-specific converse; sparse mixtures can affect expected length through testing affinity differently from squared loss.

seed_details.seed: Adaptive retained-prefix-depth oracle inequality with endogenous-target correction
seed_details.anchor_opened: arXiv:1910.06508, Introduction, conditional Monte Carlo representation, Theorem 1 and proof, finite- and infinite-horizon comparisons, and Discussion.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Derive an exact identity for conditioning the propensity-dependent likelihood ratio on a shorter prefix; unlike fixed-policy conditional importance sampling, this creates a mixed-prefix target correction before any Lepski selection.
seed_details.destination_search: Jiang--Li sequential doubly robust recursion, Kallus--Uehara marginalized ratios, and ZhouHannaZhuYangShi2025 history-dependent propensity fitting all retain Markov, parametric, or fixed-policy structure and provide no unrestricted depth oracle inequality.
seed_details.red_team: Rao--Blackwellization guarantees that a shorter retained history always improves risk.
seed_details.rebuttal: Conditioning reduces variance for a fixed unbiased target, but here shortening history alters an unknown behavior-dependent intervention and introduces bias whose first mixed-prefix term is not a conditional-variance identity.

seed_details.seed: Global-to-local efficiency breakdown radius around sparse propensity trees
seed_details.anchor_opened: arXiv:2006.03886, Introduction, tilting-policy efficient influence function, efficiency-bound comparison, non-Markov embedding, and estimator remainder proof.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: After deriving the bounded full-tree canonical gradient, replace ordinary local asymptotic normality by a growing-alphabet neighborhood modulus that locates the largest radius on which regular root-\(n\) estimation remains uniform.
seed_details.destination_search: SchindlShenKennedy2024 supplies tilt-calibrated Le Cam alternatives and ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024Discrete supplies growing-category fuzzy hypotheses, but neither derives a local-neighborhood radius for a nested natural policy.
seed_details.red_team: This merely restates that pointwise semiparametric efficiency need not imply uniform minimaxity.
seed_details.rebuttal: An explicit critical neighborhood radius and a two-sided local minimax theorem would be a new quantitative object, but it is less directly responsive than the requested all-sample frontier.

seed_details.seed: Shrinking-strength onset boundary between the natural mean and the sparse-history penalty
seed_details.anchor: Prior proposal on the stationary partially observed overlap frontier, open-ended question on shrinking overlap
seed_details.anchor_opened: Prior-proposal core at the cited open-ended question and its honest-scope boundary; the iid complete-trajectory destination was then checked against Kennedy2019JASA and SchindlShenKennedy2024.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the dependent observed-filter likelihood calculation by iid complementary-prefix mixture affinity while preserving exact cancellation at \(c=0\).
seed_details.destination_search: Kennedy2019JASA gives the exact local target expansion, SchindlShenKennedy2024 gives static tilt-dependent testing, and the paired witness gives the long-history endpoint; the intermediate onset remains unoccupied.
seed_details.red_team: A Taylor expansion around \(c=0\) immediately gives the transition.
seed_details.rebuttal: The product \(T\eta\) can diverge, unseen-prefix errors are nonuniform, and the zero-shift cancellation must survive the approximation statistic rather than only the population expansion.

seed_details.seed: Transition limit law for an occupancy-adaptive prefix estimator
seed_details.anchor_opened: arXiv:2505.22492, Introduction, Theorem 2, projection-based proof, extensions to sequential and doubly robust estimators, and closing discussion.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace their fixed-dimensional parametric Taylor expansion by a triangular-array Hoeffding decomposition for a data-dependent-order factorial statistic at the occupancy transition.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found Gaussian fixed-horizon efficient limits and Poissonized large-alphabet risk bounds, but no stable candidate normalization or unique limiting experiment for this unrestricted all-sequence transition.
seed_details.red_team: A central limit theorem is secondary until the rate and estimator are known.
seed_details.rebuttal: A non-Gaussian transition law could be valuable, but the current substrate does not identify one normalization uniformly over arbitrary \(T_n,c_n\), so this lane has no credible first-version survivor.

seed_details.seed: Data-driven choice of incremental strength with minimax welfare regret
seed_details.anchor_opened: arXiv:1907.04004, Introduction, incremental-effect curve definition, uniform-in-strength inference theorem, EAGeR analysis, and conclusion.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Promote \(c\) from a known intervention index to a decision selected from the estimated effect curve and lower-bound regret relative to the best incremental shift.
seed_details.destination_search: Policy-learning searches found empirical welfare maximization for externally indexed policy classes, not behavior-dependent policy curves whose value changes with an unrestricted unknown history tree.
seed_details.red_team: This changes the scientific target from estimating a prespecified intervention to optimizing a policy without any intervention-cost or welfare criterion in the topic.
seed_details.rebuttal: A defensible regret theorem would require an added utility or cost primitive, so it is a scope expansion and is not retained for this proposal.

seed_details.seed: Permutation or conformal inversion for a nonlinear incremental distribution functional
seed_details.anchor_opened: arXiv:math/0503662, Introduction, ordered-modulus lower theorem, interval construction, and discussion; targeted symmetry and conformal searches were then run for off-policy values.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Find a finite group action under which a null value of \(F_{T,c}(P)\) is invariant while the nuisance trajectory law remains unrestricted.
seed_details.destination_search: No exchangeability orbit was found that fixes the nonlinear propensity-dependent null across arbitrary trajectory laws; existing conformal counterfactual methods require placebo or time symmetry absent from iid trajectory sampling.
seed_details.red_team: There is no exact symmetry to invert beyond exchangeability of the sample labels, which carries no information about a nonlinear distribution functional.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds on the unrestricted class, so this lane is dropped rather than relabeled as an asymptotic interval problem.

proposed_from.literature_map: Selected full-frontier thread: KimKennedyNaimi2021 supplies the exact longitudinal incremental setup, positivity motivation, fixed-horizon identifying and influence-function constructions, and its special constant-propensity growing-horizon comparison. KallusUehara2024NaturalPolicies establishes the closest local efficiency analysis for behavior-dependent policies; MaZhuJiaoWainwright2022 establishes the closest finite-sample oracle-information separation; ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024Discrete establishes the closest causal unseen-context converse; SchindlShenKennedy2024 and HuangDongLinAntonelli2026 cover static tilt-sensitive minimax and limit theory. None subsumes the nested sequential target, and the explicit \(T=2\) law rules out a one-normalizer reduction. Selected approximation-engine thread: JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015 gives smooth--nonsmooth polynomial estimation and approximation--moment duality, MaZhuJiaoWainwright2022 adapts Chebyshev polynomials to unknown logging, RobinsLiTchetgenVanderVaart2016TR provides higher-order degenerate-\(U\)-statistic corrections, and ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024Discrete provides causal fuzzy-hypothesis constructions. Their first common failure is that they treat unrelated cells or fixed-dimensional projection kernels, whereas a legal trajectory subtree imposes nested parent-sum constraints. Honest-length thread: CaiLow2004 gives ordered-modulus expected-length lower bounds, KimKennedyNaimi2021 gives asymptotic nuisance-controlled incremental intervals, DaiEtAl2020CoinDICE gives behavior-agnostic intervals from Markov occupancy equations, and Armstrong--Kolesar bias-aware inference balances explicit bias against stochastic radius on smooth regression classes. No closer source gives minimax expected connected length for the unrestricted nonlinear trajectory functional. The M11 limit-law lane was searched through ZhouHannaZhuYangShi2025 and large-alphabet transition theory but lacked a stable normalization before the rate is known. The M16 policy-regret lane required a new welfare criterion, and the M17 symmetry lane lacked a nuisance-invariant group action; both were dropped rather than padded.

banked_reason: The proposed all-(n,T,c) matched frontier has been replaced by a long-history theorem plus an explicitly unresolved elbow, so no all-sample evaluable r/ell or complete consistency-and-oracle phase diagram is delivered.
banked_proposal_promise_gap: The factor-two logarithmic elbow remains open: no compatible-prefix estimator with controlled nested-count covariance or matching fixed-sample legal-subtree converse was delivered.
